ud6.6:19.3: Seated to one side, those mendicants said to the Buddha,
ud6.6:20.1: “Sir, several ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers who follow various other religions are residing in Sāvatthī, holding different views, beliefs, and opinions, relying on different views.
ud6.6:21.1: There were some ascetics and brahmins who had this doctrine and view:
ud6.6:21.2: ‘The self and the cosmos are eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’ …
ud6.6:21.3: They were fighting, quarreling, and disputing, continually wounding each other with barbed words:
ud6.6:21.4: ‘Such is Truth, such is not Truth!
ud6.6:21.5: Such is not Truth, such is Truth!’”
ud6.6:22.1: “Mendicants, the wanderers of other religions are blind and sightless.
ud6.6:22.2: They don’t understand what is beneficial or what is not beneficial, nor what is the truth and what is not the truth.
ud6.6:22.3: Not understanding what is beneficial or what is not beneficial, nor what is the truth and what is not the truth, they are fighting, quarreling, and disputing, continually wounding each other with barbed words:
ud6.6:22.4: ‘Such is Truth, such is not Truth!
ud6.6:22.5: Such is not Truth, such is Truth!’”
